evidence.field: 說文釋形; 漢語拼音; 釋義
evidence.text: The 囧 entry gives current Mandarin jiǒng and records two historical sound statements: Shuowen says 讀若獷, while Jia Shi Zhong reportedly said it was read like 明. The entry describes a window and cites meanings including bright. These are lexicographic reports, not independent proof of an ancient sound match between a window’s name and 明.
evidence.title: B00484 囧 — Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.text: The entry identifies 朙 as a variant of 明, gives its Mandarin reading míng, and quotes Shuowen’s analysis 月+囧 with 明 as an ancient form. This supports the stated variant relation and the historical analysis, but does not establish 朙 as the only early construction of 明.

search_audit.outcome: Search results and opened entries confirm current readings jiǒng and míng, and record the historical Shuowen/Jia Shi Zhong statements. Unihan access remains unavailable.

gaps: The exact local Unihan row correction cannot be independently checked in this web-only pass. The supplied audit reports that the local kMandarin row for 明 is míng; this finding is not repeated as external evidence.

Official Unihan pages for U+660E and U+56E7 remain inaccessible, so their required character-specific click-through verification is incomplete. The opened MOE entries independently verify current Mandarin readings.
The historical report that 囧 was read like 明 does not independently establish a phonetic relationship in 朙 or recover the ancient spoken name of the depicted window.
